description.ncbi_summary: Predicted to enable aminoacylase activity. Located in extracellular exosome. [provided by Alliance of Genome Resources, Apr 2022]

uniprot_function.text: Deacetylates N-acetyl aromatic amino acids and mercapturic acids (N-acetyl-L-cysteine-S-conjugates), including halogenated mercapturic acids derived from the metabolism of environmental contaminants such as trichloroethylene, making it a key enzyme in the processing of both endogenous and xenobiotic compounds. In neurons and blood vessels, deacetylates the mercapturates of 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4HNE) and acrolein (ACR), two highly reactive lipid peroxidation products; the resulting deacetylated products can then be transformed into toxic compounds by beta-lyase.
